query: Which was bigger, the Roman Empire or the Mongol Empire?
answer: The Mongol Empire was much bigger, about four to five times the size of the Roman Empire at its largest. At its peak in the late 13th century, the Mongol Empire covered about 24 million km² (9.3 million sq mi) and ruled roughly 110 million people. It stretched about 12,000 km from Korea to Hungary, which makes it the largest contiguous land empire in history [1][2]. The Roman Empire was at its largest under Trajan in AD 117, at about 5 million km² (some estimates say up to 5.5 million) with perhaps 50–70 million people. It held that size only briefly, because Hadrian gave up most of the eastern conquests soon after [3][4]. Rome did last much longer as a unified state, though. For total size, only the British Empire, at about 35.5 million km² spread across the oceans, beat the Mongols [2].
